ai.description: Gavi Night Frogs are small (25–30 mm) with brown, mottled skin. They possess prominent, fleshy, triangular toe tips and a distinct, pointed snout.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Gavi Night Frog is best distinguished by the distinct, fleshy, triangular webbing that extends to the tips of its toes, a feature absent in most other *Nyctibatrachus*.
ai.habitat: The Gavi Night Frog inhabits mid-to-high elevation evergreen forests in the Western Ghats, typically residing near rocky streams at altitudes between 800 and 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: The Gavi Night Frog is strictly nocturnal, remaining hidden in rock crevices or under leaf litter during the day and emerging at night to hunt for small insects.
ai.reproductionNotes: The Gavi Night Frog breeds during the monsoon, laying clutches of 20–30 eggs on wet rocks, where males provide parental care by guarding the developing embryos.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Gavi Night Frog is endemic to the southern Western Ghats in Kerala, India, typically found at elevations between 800 and 1,100 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Gavi Night Frog emits a series of high-pitched, rhythmic "ticking" or "chirping" sounds, typically heard near fast-flowing streams in its dense forest habitat.
